options.C: It uses a three-way handshake involving a Ticket Granting Service (TGS) and a session key
options.D: It performs a brute-force search of a local password database to find a matching hash

questions.explanation: NTLMv2 is more complex than v1, incorporating client-side challenges (nonces) and timestamps to prevent replay attacks.

questions.question: What are the primary security merits of using the NTLMv2 protocol?

options.A: It uses strong HMAC-MD5 hashing and is more resistant to brute-force and spoofing attacks
options.B: It is the only authentication protocol that is fully compatible with all legacy Windows systems
options.C: It eliminates the need for a centralized Domain Controller by using peer-to-peer authentication
options.D: It automatically encrypts all network traffic between the client and the server after logon

questions.explanation: The use of HMAC-MD5 and the inclusion of more variable data in the response make NTLMv2 significantly harder to attack than its predecessors.

questions.question: How many recent password hashes are typically stored by the 'Cached Credentials' feature in Windows?

options.A: The last 10 successful logons
options.B: The last 5 successful logons
options.C: Every successful logon since the system was last rebooted
options.D: Only the hash of the currently logged-on user is stored

questions.explanation: By default, Windows caches the hashes of the last 10 users who logged on locally. This allows them to log on even if a Domain Controller is unavailable.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Active Directory Group Policy?

options.A: To provide administrators with a centralized way to manage settings for users and computers
options.B: To automatically group users based on their physical location within the office
options.C: To monitor the real-time network activity of all AD-enabled devices
options.D: To provide a secure way for users to share files and folders with each other

questions.explanation: Group Policy is a powerful tool for enforcing security settings, software installation, and desktop configurations across a domain.

questions.question: Which of the following can be configured and enforced using Active Directory Group Policy?

options.A: Screen lock timeouts, USB port access, and domain password policies
options.B: The physical hardware configuration of individual workstations
options.C: The real-time routing of external internet traffic for the entire domain
options.D: The individual browser history and personal files of every domain user

questions.explanation: Administrators use Group Policy Objects (GPOs) to define and enforce these and many other settings.

questions.question: What is a Group Policy Object (GPO) in the context of Active Directory?

options.A: A virtual collection of policy settings that can be applied to users or computers
options.B: A physical server that is dedicated to storing and distributing group policies
options.C: A specialized type of user account that has been granted administrative privileges
options.D: A cryptographic key used to sign and verify the integrity of group policy updates

questions.explanation: A GPO is the container for the actual policy settings. It is linked to AD containers like Sites, Domains, or OUs.

questions.question: What does the acronym GPO stand for?

options.A: Group Policy Object
options.B: Global Password Option
options.C: General Protocol Order
options.D: Graphical Policy Organizer

questions.explanation: GPO stands for Group Policy Object.

questions.question: What is the 'Local Security Policy' on a Windows computer?

options.A: A set of security-related Group Policy settings that apply only to that specific machine
options.B: A policy that is automatically applied to all computers within the same local subnet
options.C: A specialized firewall rule that prevents unauthorized access to the local hard drive
options.D: A list of all users who have been granted permission to log on to the local machine

questions.explanation: Every Windows machine has its own local policy. In a domain environment, domain-level GPOs usually override local settings.

questions.question: Which Windows utility is used to manage the Local Security Policy?

options.A: gpedit.msc
options.B: regedit.exe
options.C: services.msc
options.D: eventvwr.msc

questions.explanation: The Group Policy Editor (gpedit.msc) is the standard tool for managing local policy settings.

questions.question: What is the standard order of precedence for applying Group Policy settings in Active Directory?

options.A: Local, Site, Domain, Parent OU, Child OU
options.B: Child OU, Parent OU, Domain, Site, Local
options.C: Domain, Site, Local, Child OU, Parent OU
options.D: Site, Domain, Local, Parent OU, Child OU

questions.explanation: This is often remembered by the acronym LSDOU. The last policy applied (the one closest to the object) wins in case of conflicts.

questions.question: What is the name of the default Group Policy that is created when a new Active Directory domain is established?

options.A: Default Domain Policy
options.B: Global Security Schema
options.C: Standard User Template
options.D: Root Forest Configuration

questions.explanation: The Default Domain Policy contains basic security settings that apply to all users and computers in the domain.

questions.question: When is the 'Default Domain Policy' typically utilized in an Active Directory environment?

options.A: When there are no other more specific Group Policies applied to an object
options.B: Only when a Domain Controller is in 'Safe Mode' or undergoing maintenance
options.C: It is the only policy that is applied to the 'Administrator' account by default
options.D: It is used to define the physical hardware requirements for all domain workstations

questions.explanation: It serves as a baseline. More specific GPOs linked to OUs will override settings in the Default Domain Policy.

questions.question: What is a 'Rainbow Table Attack' in the context of password cracking?

options.A: Using a pre-computed table of hashes and their corresponding plaintext passwords
options.B: A brute-force attack that tries every possible combination of characters in sequence
options.C: Intercepting a password hash as it is sent over the network and replaying it
options.D: Tricking a user into revealing their password through a phishing email or website

questions.explanation: Rainbow tables trade storage space for time, allowing for much faster cracking of hashes compared to traditional brute-force methods.

questions.question: What is the primary limitation of a Rainbow Table Attack?

options.A: It is limited by the size and coverage of the pre-computed rainbow table
options.B: It can only be used to crack passwords that are less than 8 characters long
options.C: It requires a high-speed internet connection to access the remote hash database
options.D: It is completely ineffective against hashes that have been 'salted'

questions.explanation: A rainbow table only contains hashes for a specific set of passwords and a specific hashing algorithm. If a password isn't in the table, it won't be found.

questions.question: In the context of security, what is the difference between the 'Definition' and 'Enforcement' of a password policy?

options.A: Definition is the guideline on requirements; Enforcement is the technology that ensures compliance
options.B: Definition is the legal requirement; Enforcement is the disciplinary action taken for violations
options.C: Definition is the software used to create passwords; Enforcement is the hardware used to store them
options.D: There is no practical difference; both terms refer to the same set of security rules

questions.explanation: A policy might define that passwords must be 12 characters long, but without technical enforcement (like GPO settings), users might not follow it.

questions.question: What is the general definition of a 'Password Policy'?

options.A: A set of rules designed to enhance security by encouraging the use of strong passwords
options.B: A list of all passwords that have been used by domain users in the past year
options.C: A specialized encryption algorithm used to protect passwords stored on a server
options.D: A legal agreement that users must sign before being granted access to the network

questions.explanation: A good password policy balances security requirements with usability.

questions.question: Which of the following are recognized industry standards for developing a robust password policy?

options.A: CIS Password Policy Guide and PCI DSS
options.B: ISO 9001 and Six Sigma
options.C: IEEE 802.11 and WPA3
options.D: GDPR and HIPAA

questions.explanation: These standards provide detailed recommendations for password length, complexity, and rotation.

questions.question: Which of the following would be considered a typical requirement in a sample corporate password policy?

options.A: Minimum 8 characters, including uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols
options.B: Passwords must be changed every 7 days and cannot be reused for 5 years
options.C: Passwords must be exactly 10 characters long and consist only of lowercase letters
options.D: The password must be identical to the user's employee identification number

questions.explanation: This is a standard 'complexity' requirement found in many organizations.

questions.question: What is a common method used by attackers to compromise the Security Account Manager (SAM) database on a Windows machine?

options.A: Dumping the database files to extract hashes and then attempting to crack them
options.B: Performing a remote SQL injection attack against the local SAM service
options.C: Using a specialized hardware device to physically read the SAM data from the disk
options.D: Tricking an administrator into providing the SAM decryption key via social engineering

questions.explanation: Tools like Mimikatz or pwdump can be used to extract hashes from the SAM file or from memory (LSASS).

questions.question: Which of the following is a common passive OS fingerprinting technique?

options.A: Monitoring network traffic using tools like Wireshark or p0f to analyze packet characteristics
options.B: Sending specifically crafted TCP/UDP packets to the target and observing the responses
options.C: Performing a full port scan using nmap with the -O flag to identify the operating system
options.D: Connecting to common services like HTTP or SSH to read the version information in the banner

questions.explanation: Passive fingerprinting does not send any traffic to the target; instead, it listens to existing traffic to identify OS signatures (like TTL or window size).

questions.question: What defines an 'active' OS fingerprinting method?

options.A: Sending probes to the target and analyzing how the OS responds to non-standard packets
options.B: Passively capturing and analyzing network traffic without interacting with the target
options.C: Searching public databases like WHOIS to find information about the server's owner
options.D: Using social engineering to trick a user into revealing their operating system version

questions.explanation: Active fingerprinting involves sending specifically crafted packets (e.g., using nmap -O) and observing how the target's TCP/IP stack responds.

questions.question: Which nmap flag is specifically used to enable Operating System detection?

options.A: -O
options.B: -sV
options.C: -sS
options.D: -Pn

questions.explanation: The -O flag triggers nmap's OS detection engine, which sends probes to open and closed ports to identify the target OS.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of 'banner grabbing' during a security assessment?

options.A: To identify infrastructure details, such as service versions, from headers and initial responses
options.B: To capture user credentials as they are transmitted in plaintext over the network
options.C: To perform a Denial of Service (DoS) attack by overwhelming the service with requests
options.D: To bypass firewall rules by masquerading as a legitimate administrative connection

questions.explanation: Banner grabbing involves connecting to a service (like web or mail) and reading the initial text string (banner) it sends, which often reveals the software version.

questions.question: How can a penetration tester most effectively identify application versions running on a network?

options.A: Using an nmap scan with the -sV flag to enable service version detection
options.B: Performing a ping sweep to see which hosts are active on the subnet
options.C: Running a traceroute to determine the network path to the target server
options.D: Using a WHOIS query to find the registrar information for the domain

questions.explanation: The -sV flag in nmap probes open ports to determine what service is running and its specific version number.

questions.question: Which command can be used to retrieve server type information from HTTP response headers?

options.A: curl -I <URL>
options.B: ping <IP>
options.C: nslookup <Domain>
options.D: traceroute <IP>

questions.explanation: The 'curl -I' command sends a HEAD request, which returns only the HTTP headers, often including the 'Server' header (e.g., Server: Apache/2.4.41).

questions.question: What is a fundamental difference between encryption and encoding?

options.A: Encryption requires a secret key for reversibility; encoding uses a public, predefined scheme
options.B: Encryption is used for data at rest; encoding is used only for data in transit
options.C: Encryption is always faster than encoding because it uses more efficient algorithms
options.D: Encoding provides a high level of confidentiality; encryption is primarily for integrity

questions.explanation: Encryption is a security measure designed to hide data (confidentiality), while encoding is a data transformation method used for compatibility (e.g., Base64).

questions.question: In cryptography, what does the process of 'encryption' involve?

options.A: Using an algorithm and a key to transform plaintext into unreadable ciphertext
options.B: Converting data into a standard format like ASCII or UTF-8 for storage
options.C: Compressing a file to reduce its size for faster transmission over a network
options.D: Adding a digital signature to a document to verify its authenticity and origin

questions.explanation: Encryption ensures that only authorized parties with the correct decryption key can read the original data.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'encoding' data?

options.A: To convert data from one form to another using a predefined scheme for compatibility
options.B: To protect sensitive information from being accessed by unauthorized users
options.C: To ensure that data has not been tampered with during transmission (integrity)
options.D: To uniquely identify the sender of a message using a private cryptographic key

questions.explanation: Encoding (like Base64 or URL encoding) is not a security mechanism; it's used to ensure data can be correctly processed by different systems.

questions.question: When comparing encoding and encryption, which factors are most significantly different?

options.A: Reversibility without a key and the primary goal (compatibility vs. confidentiality)
options.B: The length of the output and the type of character set used for the result
options.C: The requirement for a network connection and the operating system used
options.D: The cost of the software required and the level of mathematical complexity

questions.explanation: Encoding is easily reversible by anyone who knows the scheme, whereas encryption requires a secret key to reverse.

questions.question: Which of the following are common examples of encryption algorithms?

options.A: RSA and AES
options.B: Base64 and ASCII
options.C: URL and Hexadecimal
options.D: MD5 and SHA1

questions.explanation: RSA is an asymmetric encryption algorithm, while AES is a symmetric one. Base64 and ASCII are encoding schemes, and MD5/SHA1 are hashing algorithms.

questions.question: Which of the following are common examples of data encoding schemes?

options.A: Base64, ASCII, and URL encoding
options.B: RSA, AES, and Diffie-Hellman
options.C: MD5, SHA1, and HMAC
options.D: WPA2, WPA3, and TLS

questions.explanation: Encoding schemes are used for data representation and compatibility, not for securing data against unauthorized access.

questions.question: What is the primary characteristic of a cryptographic hash function?

options.A: It takes an input and returns a fixed-size string of bytes (digest) that is unique to that input
options.B: It uses a secret key to transform data into a format that can only be reversed by the key holder
options.C: It compresses large files into a smaller format while maintaining the ability to decompress them
options.D: It provides a way to verify the identity of a sender using a public and private key pair

questions.explanation: A hash is a one-way function; the same input always produces the same output, but you cannot reconstruct the input from the hash.

questions.question: Which two hashing algorithms have historically been the most widely used, despite current security concerns?

options.A: MD5 and SHA1
options.B: AES and DES
options.C: RSA and ECC
options.D: Base64 and ASCII

questions.explanation: MD5 and SHA1 were once standards for integrity checking but are now considered weak due to collision vulnerabilities.

questions.question: Are MD5 and SHA1 currently considered secure for modern cryptographic applications?

options.A: No, they are considered insecure and unsuitable for most security-sensitive applications
options.B: Yes, they remain the industry standard for securing passwords and digital signatures
options.C: Only MD5 is considered insecure; SHA1 is still widely used in high-security environments
options.D: They are only insecure if the attacker has access to a quantum computer

questions.explanation: Both MD5 and SHA1 have known vulnerabilities that allow attackers to generate collisions, making them unreliable for integrity or authenticity.

questions.question: What is the fixed output length (bit length) of an MD5 hash?

options.A: 128 bits
options.B: 160 bits
options.C: 256 bits
options.D: 512 bits

questions.explanation: MD5 always produces a 128-bit hash value, regardless of the size of the input data.

questions.question: What was the original design purpose of the MD5 hashing algorithm?

options.A: To be a cryptographic hash function for integrity checking and digital signatures
options.B: To provide a secure way to encrypt large amounts of data for storage on disk
options.C: To serve as a high-speed encoding scheme for transmitting binary data over text-based protocols
options.D: To replace the RSA algorithm as the primary method for asymmetric key exchange

questions.explanation: MD5 was designed by Ronald Rivest in 1991 to verify that a file or message had not been altered.

questions.question: Why is MD5 now considered insecure for cryptographic use?

options.A: It is susceptible to collision attacks where different inputs result in the same hash output
options.B: The algorithm is too slow for modern high-speed network communications
options.C: It requires a very large secret key that is difficult to manage and distribute securely
options.D: It can be easily reversed to reveal the original plaintext without a key

questions.explanation: Collision vulnerabilities allow attackers to create two different files that have the same MD5 hash, which can be used to bypass integrity checks.

questions.question: In the context of hashing, what is a 'collision vulnerability'?

options.A: A situation where two different inputs produce the same hash output (digest)
options.B: When two different encryption keys produce the same ciphertext for a given plaintext
options.C: An error that occurs when two network packets arrive at a switch at the exact same time
options.D: A flaw in a database that allows two users to have the same primary identification key

questions.explanation: A perfect hash function should produce a unique output for every unique input; a collision occurs when this property fails.

questions.question: What is a significant real-world risk associated with collision vulnerabilities in hashing algorithms?

options.A: Creating malicious digital certificates that appear legitimate because they share a trusted hash
options.B: Causing a server to crash by sending it two identical files with different names
options.C: Allowing an attacker to intercept and read encrypted traffic without the private key
options.D: Increasing the time it takes to verify the integrity of a large software update

questions.explanation: Attackers can use collisions to forge digital signatures or certificates, leading to a breakdown in trust for secure communications.

questions.question: What is the fixed output length (bit length) of a SHA1 hash?

options.A: 160 bits
options.B: 128 bits
options.C: 256 bits
options.D: 512 bits

questions.explanation: SHA1 always produces a 160-bit hash value, which is longer than MD5 but still considered insecure today.

questions.question: What was the primary historical use of the SHA1 hashing algorithm?

options.A: SSL/TLS certificates and file integrity validation
options.B: Encrypting high-speed data streams for wireless networks
options.C: Generating public and private key pairs for RSA encryption
options.D: Encoding binary files for transmission over email protocols

questions.explanation: SHA1 was widely used for digital signatures and certificates until its vulnerabilities became well-documented.

questions.question: Why is SHA1 now considered insecure for modern cryptographic applications?

options.A: Researchers have demonstrated that two different inputs can produce the same hash output (collisions)
options.B: The algorithm is too computationally expensive for modern web servers to process
options.C: It requires a very large secret key that is easily intercepted by attackers
options.D: It can be easily reversed to reveal the original plaintext without any key

questions.explanation: Like MD5, SHA1 is vulnerable to collision attacks, which undermines its reliability for integrity and authenticity.

questions.question: Is the SHA1 algorithm currently considered secure for protecting sensitive data?

options.A: No, it is considered insecure due to the feasibility of generating collisions
options.B: Yes, it remains the most secure hashing algorithm for all modern applications
options.C: Yes, but only if it is used in conjunction with a strong symmetric encryption key
options.D: It is only insecure if the input data is less than 1024 bytes in length

questions.explanation: Modern security standards have moved away from SHA1 in favor of more robust algorithms like SHA-256.

questions.question: Is the SHA1 hashing algorithm considered 'breakable' by modern standards?

options.A: Yes, the cost and time required to generate collisions have decreased significantly
options.B: No, it is still mathematically impossible to find two inputs with the same hash
options.C: Only if the attacker has access to the original source code of the algorithm
options.D: It can only be broken if the hash is intercepted during a man-in-the-middle attack

questions.explanation: Well-funded attackers can now generate SHA1 collisions, making it possible to forge signatures and bypass security checks.

questions.question: What is the current NIST recommendation regarding the use of the SHA1 algorithm?

options.A: NIST advises against using SHA1 in favor of stronger algorithms like SHA-256 or SHA-3
options.B: NIST recommends SHA1 as the primary method for securing all government communications
options.C: NIST suggests using SHA1 only for data that is encrypted with a 2048-bit RSA key
options.D: NIST has no official recommendation regarding SHA1, as it is considered an obsolete standard

questions.explanation: NIST has officially deprecated SHA1 for most uses due to its known security weaknesses.

questions.question: What is a Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC)?

options.A: A MAC that uses a cryptographic hash function and a secret key to provide integrity and authenticity
options.B: A specialized encryption algorithm used to protect passwords stored in a local database
options.C: A method for compressing data before it is hashed to reduce the size of the final digest
options.D: A protocol used to exchange public keys between two parties over an insecure channel

questions.explanation: HMAC combines a hash function (like SHA-256) with a secret key, ensuring that only someone with the key can verify the message's integrity.

questions.question: In the context of HMAC, what does the acronym 'MAC' stand for?

options.A: Message Authentication Code
options.B: Media Access Control
options.C: Mandatory Access Control
options.D: Master Authentication Certificate

questions.explanation: A MAC is a short piece of information used to authenticate a message and confirm that it has not been modified.

questions.question: What is the primary function of an HMAC in secure communications?

options.A: To verify that the payload has not been tampered with and was sent by a trusted party
options.B: To encrypt the entire message so that it cannot be read by unauthorized intermediaries
options.C: To uniquely identify the physical device that sent the message using its hardware address
options.D: To provide a way to recover the original message if it is corrupted during transmission

questions.explanation: HMAC provides both integrity and authenticity by requiring a secret key that is known only to the sender and recipient.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) Model?

options.A: To provide a standard reference for how different technical systems communicate over a network
options.B: To define the specific hardware requirements for building a local area network (LAN)
options.C: To serve as a legal framework for regulating international telecommunications services
options.D: To replace the TCP/IP protocol suite as the primary method for internet communication

questions.explanation: The OSI model breaks down network communication into seven layers, ensuring compatibility between different vendors and technologies.

questions.question: What are the seven layers of the OSI Model in correct order from Layer 1 to Layer 7?

options.A: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
options.B: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
options.C: Physical, Network, Data Link, Transport, Presentation, Session, Application
options.D: Link, Internet, Transport, Application, Session, Presentation, Physical

questions.explanation: The OSI model layers are often remembered using mnemonics like 'Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away'.

questions.question: What are the four layers of the TCP/IP Model?

options.A: Link, Internet, Transport, Application
options.B: Physical, Network, Transport, Session
options.C: Data Link, Network, Transport, Application
options.D: Link, Network, Session, Presentation

questions.explanation: The TCP/IP model is more streamlined than the OSI model, collapsing several layers into the Application and Link layers.

questions.question: What is Layer 3 of the OSI Model, and what is its primary responsibility?

options.A: Network Layer; it handles the transfer of data packets from node to node across different networks
options.B: Transport Layer; it ensures reliable end-to-end communication and error recovery
options.C: Data Link Layer; it manages physical addressing (MAC) and media access control
options.D: Physical Layer; it defines the electrical and mechanical specifications for the network medium

questions.explanation: The Network Layer (L3) is where routing occurs, using IP addresses to move data between different network segments.

questions.question: In a common analogy comparing network addressing to postal mail, what does the IP address (IPv4/IPv6) represent?

options.A: The unique postal address and suburb of the building where the receiver is located
options.B: The specific floor and apartment number where the individual lives
options.C: The name of the person who is intended to receive the physical letter
options.D: The type of vehicle used by the postal service to deliver the mail

questions.explanation: IP addresses provide the logical location of a host on a network, similar to a street address in the physical world.

questions.question: In the postal mail analogy for network addressing, what does the MAC address represent?

options.A: The exact floor and apartment number of the receiver within a building
options.B: The city and state where the mail is being sent from
options.C: The weight and size of the envelope being delivered
options.D: The specific post office that is responsible for the final delivery

questions.explanation: A MAC address is a unique hardware identifier for a specific network interface, similar to a specific room in a building.

questions.question: How many 'octets' (8-bit groups) are contained in a standard IPv4 address?

options.A: 4 octets
options.B: 8 octets
options.C: 16 octets
options.D: 32 octets

questions.explanation: An IPv4 address consists of four groups of 8 bits each, separated by dots (e.g., 192.168.1.1).

questions.question: What is the total number of binary digits (bits) in a standard IPv4 address?

options.A: 32 bits
options.B: 64 bits
options.C: 128 bits
options.D: 256 bits

questions.explanation: Since there are 4 octets and each octet is 8 bits, the total length is 4 * 8 = 32 bits.

questions.question: In an 8-bit binary octet of an IPv4 address, what are the decimal values of each bit position in descending order?
questions.explanation: These values are powers of 2 (2^7 down to 2^0), used to convert binary octets into decimal format.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a 'Subnet Mask' in IP networking?

options.A: To define which part of an IP address represents the network and which part represents the host
options.B: To hide the internal IP addresses of a network from external attackers on the internet
options.C: To assign a unique name to a network segment for easier identification by administrators
options.D: To encrypt the headers of IP packets to prevent them from being read by unauthorized users

questions.explanation: The subnet mask uses binary 1s to identify the network portion and 0s to identify the host portion of an address.

questions.question: If a subnet mask is set to 255.255.0.0, can the first two octets of an IP address in that subnet (e.g., 192.168.x.x) ever change while remaining in the same network?

options.A: No, because the bits in the subnet mask set to 255 (all 1s) define the fixed network portion
options.B: Yes, the subnet mask only defines the range of available addresses, not which bits are fixed
options.C: Only if the router is configured to use dynamic host configuration protocol (DHCP)
options.D: Yes, but only if the network is using IPv6 instead of the standard IPv4 addressing

questions.explanation: A subnet mask of 255.255.0.0 means the first 16 bits are the network address and cannot change for hosts within that same network.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between the TCP and UDP transport protocols?

options.A: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable, while UDP is connectionless and 'best-effort'
options.B: TCP is used for local area networks, while UDP is used for wide area networks
options.C: TCP is faster than UDP because it does not require any error checking or sequencing
options.D: TCP uses 32-bit addresses, while UDP uses 128-bit addresses for identifying hosts

questions.explanation: TCP ensures data arrives correctly and in order, whereas UDP prioritizes speed and low overhead for real-time applications like streaming.

questions.question: What is the standard port number used for unencrypted web traffic via HTTP?

options.A: Port 80
options.B: Port 443
options.C: Port 21
options.D: Port 22

questions.explanation: Port 80 is the default for HTTP, though it is increasingly being replaced by the more secure HTTPS on port 443.

questions.question: What is the standard port number used for secure web traffic via HTTPS?

options.A: Port 443
options.B: Port 80
options.C: Port 22
options.D: Port 25

questions.explanation: HTTPS uses SSL/TLS to encrypt communication between a client and a server, typically over port 443.

questions.question: Which port is commonly used for the control channel of the File Transfer Protocol (FTP)?

options.A: Port 21
options.B: Port 20
options.C: Port 22
options.D: Port 23

questions.explanation: FTP uses port 21 for commands and port 20 for the actual data transfer in active mode.

questions.question: What is the standard port number for Secure Shell (SSH) remote access?

options.A: Port 22
options.B: Port 23
options.C: Port 25
options.D: Port 53

questions.explanation: SSH provides a secure, encrypted alternative to Telnet for remote command-line access, using port 22.

questions.question: Which port was historically used for unencrypted remote terminal access via Telnet?

options.A: Port 23
options.B: Port 22
options.C: Port 21
options.D: Port 25

questions.explanation: Telnet is insecure because it sends data (including passwords) in plain text; it uses port 23.

questions.question: What is the standard port number for the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP)?

options.A: Port 25
options.B: Port 110
options.C: Port 143
options.D: Port 587

questions.explanation: SMTP is used for sending emails between servers, traditionally over port 25.

questions.question: Which port is used by the Domain Name System (DNS) for standard name resolution queries?

options.A: Port 53
options.B: Port 67
options.C: Port 68
options.D: Port 80

questions.explanation: DNS translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses, primarily using UDP port 53.

questions.question: Which ports are used by the Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP)?

options.A: Ports 67 and 68
options.B: Ports 53 and 54
options.C: Ports 80 and 443
options.D: Ports 161 and 162

questions.explanation: DHCP uses port 67 for the server and port 68 for the client to automatically assign IP addresses.

questions.question: What is the standard port number for the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP)?

options.A: Port 3389
options.B: Port 3306
options.C: Port 5432
options.D: Port 5900

questions.explanation: RDP allows users to remotely control a Windows computer over a network, typically using port 3389.

questions.question: What is the standard port number used by the MySQL database management system?

options.A: Port 3306
options.B: Port 1433
options.C: Port 5432
options.D: Port 1521

questions.explanation: MySQL is one of the most popular open-source relational databases and defaults to port 3306.

questions.question: Which port does MariaDB typically use for its database services?

options.A: Port 3306
options.B: Port 3307
options.C: Port 1433
options.D: Port 5432

questions.explanation: MariaDB was created as a fork of MySQL and maintains compatibility by using the same default port, 3306.

questions.question: What is the standard port number for Microsoft SQL Server (MSSQL)?

options.C: Port 3306
options.D: Port 1521

questions.explanation: MSSQL is a proprietary relational database from Microsoft and defaults to port 1433 for its main instance.

options.A: Port 1521
options.B: Port 1522
options.C: Port 1433
options.D: Port 3306

questions.explanation: The Oracle TNS listener manages incoming connection requests to an Oracle database, typically on port 1521.

options.D: Port 1433

options.B: Port 27018

options.B: Port 6380

options.D: Port 3306

questions.explanation: Redis is often used as a database, cache, and message broker, defaulting to port 6379.

options.C: Port 7199

questions.explanation: Cassandra uses port 9042 for its native binary protocol (CQL), which is the primary client interface.
